connector: Knights in stories always seem brave and perfect. Today’s article tells how a boy really became a knight, one step at a time, and what knights were supposed to be like. Look for why each step came before the next.

a.raw: sir henry trained as a squire in kent
a.why: Sir is a title right before his name, Henry, so both get capitals. Kent is the name of a place. Squire is not a name, so it stays small. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: the young page served lady margaret at windsor castle
b.why: The starts the sentence. Lady is a title right before her name, Margaret. Windsor Castle is the name of one castle. A period ends the sentence.

vcloze1.h1: Find the word for the code of rules knights were supposed to follow.
vcloze1.why: Chivalry was the code: be brave, loyal and kind to the weak.

vcloze2.h1: This young helper polished armor and cared for the horse.
vcloze2.why: A squire served a knight while training to become one.

vcloze3.h1: Find the word for being made a knight with a tap of the sword.
vcloze3.why: To be dubbed is to be made a knight in a ceremony.

vcloze4.h1: Find the word for a contest where knights showed their skill.
vcloze4.why: A tournament was a contest of knights before a crowd.

match.chivalry: Chivalry is a set of rules. Look for the meaning about a code.
match.squire: A squire is a person. Look for the meaning about helping a knight.
match.dubbed: Dubbed is something that happens to you. Look for the meaning about the sword on the shoulder.
match.tournament: A tournament is an event. Look for the meaning about a contest.

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Squire
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A squire was a teenage boy training to be a knight, often from about age fourteen.
He cleaned his knight’s armor, cared for his horses, and helped him dress for battle.
He practiced with sword, shield and lance almost every day, often for several years.

transcripts.welcome: Welcome back, it’s Opti. How did a boy become a knight? Not overnight! Today’s article tells the steps, in order.
transcripts.guide1: Word study. Match script and scribe words, find main ideas, and hunt for endings.
transcripts.guide2: Read about knights. Then watch my video in the Read Like a Writer box.
transcripts.guide3: Today you fix your paragraph so every sentence fits your topic.

notes.wordParts: The root script or scribe means write. describe = to write about something. manuscript = written by hand. One root, two spellings.
notes.grammar: A paragraph has one main idea, often in the first sentence (the topic sentence). The other sentences are details that support it. A sentence that does not support it is off the topic.
notes.spelling: -ful means full of (hopeful). -less means without (hopeless). -ness turns a describing word into a thing (kindness). -ly tells how something was done (quickly).
notes.wgrd: Look for why each step happens. A boy became a page, then a squire, then a knight. Each step got him ready for the next.
vocab: the code of honorable behavior for knights
a young man serving a knight while training to become one
made a knight in a ceremony, with the tap of a sword on the shoulder
a contest where knights competed to show their skill

mods.script: Be a suffix detective. Which word means without? Mindful. Breathless. Fondness. Softly. Breathless! Breath, plus less: without breath. Read the rule. Then in each row, tap the one word with the ending named above it.

Some knights broke the rules of chivalry. Part two, read like a writer. It's short, and In reality warns you a surprise is coming: the truth, not the story. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: In reality, not every owl stays up all night. Now it's your turn with the sentence about years of training. Write one sentence in each box.

virtue.name: diligence
virtue.title: Diligence Watch: Is someone working hard?

items.t: A squire cared for a knight's armor and horse, and trained with sword and horse.
items.why: Caring for armor and training every day is hard, steady work.

items.t: Becoming a knight took years of training.
In reality, not every knight followed the code.
items.why: That is about knights breaking rules, not about someone working hard.
